newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Tung rejects calls to ban Chinese funds.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tung rejects calls to ban Chinese funds.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa, who plans to outlaw foreign donations to local political groups, is set to reject a demand to extend the ban to include China, a Hong Kong newspaper said on Tuesday.
The South China Morning Post quoted sources as saying moves to ban mainland political donations could not be accepted because Hong Kong and China would soon be "one country".
Hong Kong, a British colony for 156 years, reverts to China at midnight on June 30, only 49 days away.
Tung launched a three-week exercise in April to tap public views on his plan to bar funding from overseas and limit the right to protests.
Tung and his inner cabinet, the Executive Council, would finalise the plans in their Tuesday's meeting, the Post said, adding details would be announced on Thursday.
Pro-democracy movement and lawyers in the territory have slammed the proposals.
During the consultation periods, a pro-China trade union suggested the ban on foreign donations should include China's ruling Communist Party.
However, the newspaper said the ban would apply to Taiwan, which is being regarded by Beijing as renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949.
Officials from Tung's office were not immediately available for comment.
